title: Ollama 0.6.6 leaves runner processes and VRAM allocated after models disappear from ollama ps
body: For the last few weeks, VRAM has remained in use after an LLM was used, even though `ollama ps` shows nothing. I first noticed it with `deepseek-coder-v2:16b` and a derived model whose Modelfile sets `num_ctx 24576` and `num_predict 8192`. I am running Ollama 0.6.6 on Linux with an Nvidia GPU and AMD CPU. I believe this also happened on 0.6.5 and 0.6.4.

symptoms_visible: After deepseek-coder-v2:16b or its Modelfile-derived model is used, GPU memory remains occupied while `ollama ps` shows no active model.
N0.label: N0 retained VRAM reported

symptoms_visible: The same retained-resource behavior occurs with qwen2.5-coder:32b and phi4:14b as well as deepseek-coder-v2.
Process listings show runner processes that are children of the active `ollama serve` process even when fewer or no models appear in `ollama ps`; GPU memory remains occupied.
N1.label: N1 hidden runners and load-unload sequence collected

symptoms_visible: The issue is observed during normal shared use, especially while users exercise Visual Studio Code Continue features, but a simple Python streaming API script does not reproduce it.
No known client intentionally sends `keep_alive`; requests pass through an nginx reverse proxy.
N2.label: N2 workload and client pattern narrowed

symptoms_visible: A detector script repeatedly reports more `ollama runner` processes than models listed by `ollama ps`, including four runners while only one model is active.
The debug journal contains about 1,220,404 `expired event with positive ref count, retrying` entries over roughly 26.5 hours.
N3.label: N3 persistent scheduler and process mismatch documented

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Ollama 0.6.7, the detector still reports two runner processes for one active model, with the older runner continuing to occupy resources.
N4.label: N4 version 0.6.7 test unchanged

symptoms_visible: On Ollama 0.6.8, the detector again reports two runner processes for one active model.
The PID of the older retained runner does not appear in the new scheduler log lines.
N5.label: N5 early-startup failure isolated with 0.6.8 logging

symptoms_visible: Ollama 0.7.0 still shows the problem: examples include three runner processes for one active model and one runner process while `ollama ps` is empty.
N6.label: N6 version 0.7.0 test still fails

symptoms_visible: With `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`, Ollama 0.7.0 again leaves two or three runner processes while only one model is listed, and the retained process PIDs can be matched against the overlapping server logs.
N7.label: N7 decisive PID-correlated debug evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Ollama 0.7.1, the reporter observes no extra hidden runners for about two days and later confirms that the problem has not returned.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on 0.7.1

question_patterns: Does this only happen with deepseek-coder-v2, or do other models show it too?
Which other models have left memory allocated?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It also happened with qwen2.5-coder:32b and phi4:14b, in addition to both the original and Modelfile-derived deepseek-coder-v2:16b.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Only the Modelfile-derived deepseek model shows it; the original and all other models unload normally.

question_patterns: What does the requested `ps` command show while the VRAM is still allocated?
Are runner processes still alive when `ollama ps` is empty?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The service is running and the process listing shows child `ollama runner` processes. Later `ollama ps` shows nothing while a runner remains and VRAM is still used.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No runner process remains; only the Nvidia driver reports cached memory after every Ollama process has exited.
Two runners remain instead of one, but the same mismatch with `ollama ps` is present.

question_patterns: Can you enable `OLLAMA_DEBUG` and provide server logs covering the event?
What happens in the logs when the hidden runner starts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The logs show a runner starting, a health request receiving connection refused shortly before the runner begins listening, the model being marked to expire or unload, and the runner continuing to load and serve.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The server log ends in a fatal crash before the runner becomes ready, and the surviving runner is reparented to PID 1.

edges.comment: Comments c4-c15 collect debug logs, affected models, process listings, and the first evidence that load and unload actions overlap while the main server remains active.

question_patterns: Do your requests set `keep_alive`?
Is any client explicitly changing the model keep-alive duration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: As far as I know, no one sets `keep_alive`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every request explicitly sets `keep_alive` to an effectively infinite duration.

question_patterns: How do clients connect to Ollama?
Is there a proxy or model-preloading setup involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Clients use an nginx reverse proxy with long timeouts and buffering disabled. Models are normally preloaded into RAM for performance.

question_patterns: What client activity is happening when this occurs?
Can you narrow it down to a particular application or request pattern?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It occurs when users work in Visual Studio Code with the Continue plugin and use its AI features. Open WebUI can send one prompt to multiple models, but that did not reproduce it for me.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It reproduces with one sequential curl request using a fixed context size and no cancellation.
The VS Code theme is configured to dark mode.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce it with a small direct API script?
Does your Python streaming test trigger the extra runner?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. My Python script making streaming API calls could not reproduce the issue.

edges.comment: Comments c16-c23 and c31 narrow the workload to shared Continue usage rather than an explicit keep_alive setting or a simple isolated API call.

question_patterns: Can you capture the process mismatch when it happens?
Can you provide a repeatable way to detect, even if not trigger, the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I wrote a bash detector that compares active models from `ollama ps` with `ollama runner` processes. It detected four runners while only one model was active. The script detects the state; it does not trigger it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The detector finds two runners for one active model rather than four for one.

question_patterns: Are there repeated scheduler messages around the affected model?
How often does the expired-event retry message occur?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The journal contains 1,220,404 `expired event with positive ref count, retrying` lines in about 26.5 hours, repeatedly showing refCount=1.

edges.comment: Comments c22-c24 and c28-c30 establish an objective detector and the unusually high scheduler retry volume without claiming the detector reproduces the race.

question_patterns: Is the behavior any better after upgrading to 0.6.7?
Please test 0.6.7 and compare `ollama ps` with the runner count.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No change. On 0.6.7 the detector shows one active model but two runner processes, with an older runner identified as the candidate occupying resources.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After upgrading to 0.6.7, repeated Continue workloads never leave an extra runner and VRAM is released normally.

edges.comment: Comments c25-c27: testing 0.6.7 is a handler-requested version measurement. It falsifies the idea that the scheduler startup change in 0.6.7 resolved this case.

question_patterns: Can you install 0.6.8, enable its PID logging, and send logs when the issue recurs?
Does the retained runner PID appear in the 0.6.8 scheduler logs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On 0.6.8 the detector again found two runners for one active model. The offending older PID did not appear in the scheduler log at all.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The retained PID appears throughout the scheduler log, including a successful shutdown request and confirmed process exit.

edges.comment: Comments c33-c39: 0.6.8 adds PID-oriented diagnostics. From the missing PID, the engineer infers that the retained runner is lost during very early startup.

question_patterns: After installing 0.7.0, does the mismatch still occur?
Please verify whether 0.7.0 stops the extra runner processes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The problem remains on 0.7.0. I observed three runners for one active model, and on another day one runner remained while `ollama ps` showed zero active models.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: 0.7.0 has run under the same workload for several weeks without a runner-count mismatch.
Only two runners remain for one active model, but the same mismatch still occurs.

edges.comment: Comments c43-c49: the expected next-release change did not fully solve the case in 0.7.0. Non-debug logs lacked the necessary PIDs, so additional debug capture was required.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily run 0.7.0 with `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1` and capture logs overlapping the retained PIDs?
Do the debug logs contain the PIDs from the detector output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. With debug enabled, the detector caught three runners for one active model and the relevant runner PIDs were present in the overlapping logs. The maintainer confirmed the capture was sufficient and said debug logging could be disabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug run never reproduces the mismatch, so there are no retained PIDs to correlate.

edges.comment: Comments c50-c53 provide the decisive PID-correlated debug capture. Engineer analysis combines it with prior logs: many concurrent requests with varying context sizes cause frequent reloads, while clients abort before loading finishes, exposing an early runner-startup scheduler race.

solution.intent: Fix the scheduler's early runner-startup lifecycle race so concurrent reloads and request cancellation cannot leave a runner outside scheduler tracking, release the fix in Ollama 0.7.1, and require the reporter to verify it under the real Continue workload before closing.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the scheduler/runner startup path so a runner being loaded or replaced remains tracked and is terminated when concurrent varying-context requests are aborted; ship the change in v0.7.1, then monitor the real shared VS Code Continue workload and confirm that runner counts continue to match `ollama ps` before declaring resolution.

edges.comment: Comments c42-c57: the maintainer identifies the concurrency/context-size/cancellation race, ships the fix in 0.7.1, and the reporter verifies first after roughly two days and again later that the problem has not returned.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true cause as an Ollama scheduler/runner lifecycle race during very early runner startup: many concurrent requests with varying context sizes trigger model reloads while clients abort before loading completes, allowing a runner to continue outside scheduler tracking and retain resources.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: live child runner processes outnumber models in `ollama ps`, load and unload overlap around startup/health checks, the 0.6.8 offending PID is absent from scheduler logs, and the later debug capture correlates retained PIDs with scheduling activity.

Must not describe this as the already-fixed Gemma 3 classical memory leak, an intentional `keep_alive`, or merely an orphan caused by the main server being killed; the retained runners are observed beneath a live `ollama serve` process.
Must not claim that upgrading to 0.6.7 or 0.7.0 resolved the case, because the reporter reproduced the runner-count mismatch on both versions.

The resolution must fix tracking and cleanup in the early runner-startup scheduler path, identify Ollama 0.7.1 as the fixed release, and require verification under the reporter's real concurrent VS Code Continue workload.
Must declare the issue resolved only after the reporter confirms that 0.7.1 runs without recurrence, including the later follow-up that the problem has not returned.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Linux administrator and technical Ollama operator. Comfortable editing systemd environment settings, configuring nginx, inspecting processes and journald logs, writing Bash and Python diagnostic scripts, comparing PIDs, and testing multiple releases.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, cooperative, and evidence-driven. Provides commands, logs, process listings, screenshots, and repeated version checks; communicates in concise non-native English and asks direct questions about release timing.
